subject: Performance SLO + Concurrency requirements — follow-up and pilot quota proposal
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Oct 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO + Concurrency requirements — notes & next steps

Thanks for the time today, Jordan — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of requirements (as discussed)
- Latency targets: P95 generation latency <= 300ms for short completions (<= 64 tokens). For streaming/chat flows we need stable chunk latency ~100-200ms.
- Throughput & concurrency: expected steady-state traffic ~200-400 QPS, with peak bursts up to ~3k concurrent short requests during heavy events.
- Concurrency model: multiple backend services will open pooled connections (approx 20-50 sockets per service instance); we expect ~120-250 parallel in-flight requests across our cluster during pilot.
- Streaming: we’ll use streaming responses for chat UI with long-lived connections (20-120s) and intermittent bursts of new connections on page loads.
- Other: token throughput budget for pilot ~3-6M tokens/day, with burst token/sec requirements during events.

Action items / next steps
1) Marissa: will send a pilot quota proposal (concurrency + rate-limit profile) and a short quote for a 90-day pilot.
2) Jordan: send the security questionnaire and procurement timeline (Procurement contact copied).
3) Naomi: to share recommended connection-pooling guidance for our client-side SDK and any streaming best-practices.

Attachments: acme-performance-slo-notes-20271025.docx (call notes)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a pilot quota suggestion by end of week.

—
Marissa Cole

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>

Cc: DevOps Team <devops@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO + Concurrency requirements — notes & next steps

Appreciate the recap, Marissa — this matches our expectations. A couple clarifying points so your quota proposal is aligned with our needs: 

1) Burst concurrency: those 3k concurrent short requests are real for product launches (they typically last ~2-10 minutes). We can accept a soft limit with graceful throttling, but we want to avoid connection resets.
2) Connection pooling: each of our services keeps roughly 25-40 keep-alive HTTP/2 connections open to the endpoint; we have ~12 service instances actively sending requests. That suggests we will have ~300-500 pooled connections to your endpoint in peak conditions.
3) Streaming specifics: streaming sessions are long-lived (30-90s) and include periodic heartbeats; we need to ensure the platform doesn’t rehydrate model state in a way that blows CPU/token cost.
4) Rate limits we care about: per-client concurrent requests, per-token/sec ingestion & egress caps, and sustained requests/minute.

Procurement timeline: our legal/procurement requested an initial pilot quote + statement of work to fast-track approval. If you can include a short note about rollback/fallback behavior (how Redwood will degrade to lower-capacity variants), that will help us sign off faster.

Would you be able to increase pilot concurrency above your default hosted limits? We want to avoid building an in-house fallback during the short pilot.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
Engineering Manager, Product Infrastructure | Acme
jordan.lee@acme.com

Subject: Fwd: Acme — concurrency asks and procurement request

Laura/Naomi — forwarding Jordan’s note and my read on quota options. Key asks: stronger pilot concurrency (handle ~3k short bursts), support for 300-500 pooled connections, streaming-friendly token throughput, and a short SOW for procurement.

Proposed pilot quota (internal recommendation)
- Concurrent requests cap (soft): 250 dedicated concurrent requests for the tenant (with a higher burst buffer gated by graceful throttling and queueing).
- Connection limit: allow 600 simultaneous HTTP connections for the tenant (to accommodate pooling across instances).
- Requests/minute: 12,000 RPM peak for the tenant during pilot windows.
- Token throughput: 3,000 tokens/sec sustained (with per-minute burst up to 10,000 tokens/sec for short periods).
- Streaming: no additional per-connection CPU re-init; maintain KV/ prefix cache for session continuity.

Fallback / reliability approach
- Canary route: route 10% traffic to a lower-capacity model variant if the main cluster hits a hard limit.
- Graceful throttling: return 429 with Retry-After on sustained overload, with an application-level header describing partial completion (so UI can fallback to cached reply).

Commercial approach
- 90-day pilot priced as a committed burst window; include a one-time setup fee for capacity reservation (details in draft quote).
- Work with Naomi for any streaming SDK guidance we should include in the onboarding plan.

Attachments: draft quote (internal) — ACME_pilot_quote_20271030.pdf (will attach final to external).

Thoughts? If you agree, I’ll send the proposal + DocuSign link to Jordan and loop in Legal/Revenue for the pilot SOW.

—
Marissa

Subject: Pilot quota proposal & SOW — Acme / Redwood pilot (90 days)

Hi Jordan — following up with the pilot proposal and next steps. Attached is a short quote + SOW for a 90-day pilot and the proposed quota profile. Highlights below so you don’t need to open the PDF immediately: 

Proposed pilot profile (tenant-scoped)
• Soft concurrent requests cap: 250 (soft limit) with a 2x short-term burst buffer handled by queueing and graceful 429s to avoid connection resets.
• Tenant connection allowance: 600 simultaneous HTTP/2 connections to support pooling across service instances.
• Peak requests/minute: up to 12,000 RPM during scheduled launch windows.
• Token throughput: 3,000 tokens/sec sustained; burst allowance up to 10,000 tokens/sec for short periods (minutes).
• Streaming: supported with preserved KV cache and no per-connection model re-init; chunk latency target remains ~100-200ms.

Operational & rollback notes
• Canary routing: we will route 10% traffic to a lower-cost model variant if we detect sustained saturation on the primary cluster.
• Observability: Redwood Console will provide per-route latency, token burn, and connection-level metrics. We’ll also expose a tenant-level quota dashboard during the pilot.
• Support: 24/7 on-call for pilot windows; named CSM during the 90-day pilot (contact Naomi).

Commercials & next steps
1) Attached quote + SOW (ACME_pilot_quote_20271030.pdf). Please share Procurement’s preferred DocuSign contact and we’ll route the SOW for signature.
2) Pre-onboard: Naomi to share SDK connection-pooling guidance and streaming best-practices.
3) Kickoff: schedule a technical onboarding call next week to finalize traffic patterns and rollout windows.

Let me know if any of the proposed numbers need to be higher for your launch — we can escalate quota with Capacity (Laura) to accommodate one-off promotions.

Thanks and looking forward —
Marissa Cole
